evidence.note: Upfront orientation: reads scaffolding (header, harness, Makefile, test.sh) and the full RFC in ordered sections before coding — shows the agent grounded the problem, but no explicit subsystem milestone plan or done-conditions are articulated in the action log.

A single large apply_patch implements the bulk of the decoder in one push before the first build. This is a monolithic-leaning approach rather than landing frame-parse → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences as independently-checkable increments.
Gets test.sh / simple + repetitive inputs decoding correctly first — an implicit 'this class works now' checkpoint that reflects a sensible easy-first ordering before tackling the compressed input.

An extended debug loop concentrated on a single compressed input (audio.wav.zst) across dozens of edit/make/run cycles. Progress is organized by test input, not by explicit per-subsystem milestones with dedicated smallest-possible test cases.

reasoning: The observable behavior shows a sensible implicit ordering — thorough recon, then simple/raw inputs green as a checkpoint, then the FSE/Huffman/sequences-heavy compressed input — which sits above the 'no ordering / just write more code' level-3 anchor. But the decoder was largely written in one big patch (step 25) and then debugged input-by-input rather than landing distinct subsystems each behind an explicit done-condition, so it falls short of the level-5 'each subsystem landed before moving on with a checkpoint' and the level-8 explicit walking-skeleton structure. This places it at a 4. Confidence is low because the trajectory is an action-only log without the agent's planning prose, which is where milestone articulation would most clearly appear.
